chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a woman who dies while the child is moving in her womb: should her abdomen be cut open and her child extracted? He said, “Yes.”

key_terms.يَتَحَرَّكُ: is moving, indicating signs of life

ai.seo_question: If a pregnant woman dies while the baby is still moving, should the child be surgically extracted?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a deceased pregnant woman whose child is still moving in her womb. It indicates that her abdomen may be opened in order to extract the child, showing the juristic treatment of such a case at the time of death.
